la: el/la — the (fem.); her/it (object pronoun) · also la que 'the one that' (Çelfa la que dizen de Canal 'Çelfa, the one they call of the Canal')
de: de — of, from · also de — by (the agent with a passive participle; = por) · also de — 'by (night)' (de noch), partitive 'of, among' (quinze moros … de los que alcançava; pocas de gentes), 'as' (de ganançia 'as booty'), 'from outside' (de fuera), 'on the right' (de diestro) · also 'about, concerning' (de mí non digan mal 'let them not speak ill of me') · also de — 'as if in' (commo de arrancada 'as if in rout'); 'in the manner of' (de guisa 'in such a way'); 'of, among' (de bivos pocos 'of the living few'); nominalized infinitive (del prender 'of the taking') · also de — 'with' of manner (de fuertes coraçones 'with stout hearts'); 'on' (de pie 'on foot'); 'from' of side (della e della part 'from both sides'); de cabo 'anew' (de + cabo, 'again'); de suso de 'above'; seños … de seños colpes 'with one blow each' · also de — 'in respect of' after an adjective (sobejana de mala 'exceedingly bad'); 'with regard to, about' (me plaze de mio Çid 'I am pleased about the Cid'); 'from, at the hand of' (de señor non ha graçia 'he gets no favor from a lord'); 'from' of origin (de moros fo 'it came from Moors'); 'at' of manner (de vagar 'at leisure', de + the noun vagar) · also de’ — Pidal's de’llaño, read as del llaño 'of the plain' (the article's l run into the ll; a reading, not certain) · de + infinitive after an adjective (de ir somos guisados 'we are ready to go')
mio: mio — my (unstressed possessive; mio Çid 'my lord Cid')
çid: Çid — the Cid, 'lord' (Arabic sīdī 'my lord'; pronounced Tsid)
el: el — the (masc.) · also el — 'he who' before a relative (el qui quisiere, el que es sobre Fenares); el before a fem. noun beginning with a vowel (el espada = la espada; el algara = la algara) · also el de + place name 'he of, the one from' (mio Çid el de Bivar)
bivar: Bivar — Vivar, the Cid's home village just north of Burgos
poblado: poblado — inhabited place, settlement (noun from poblar; = poblado) · also poblar — settled, encamped (past part.; avie poblado 'had settled, camped')
ha: aver — he has (3rd sg. present; = ha) · ha — to (a with h-, aver a + inf. 'will, must': lo an todos ha far 'all are to do it'); aver — has, possesses (las fijas que ha 'the daughters she has') · also ha — future ending after infinitive + clitics, the split future (tornar nos la ha 'he will give it back to us'; = nos la tornará) · also ha — there is, there are (impersonal; dos señas ha cabdales 'there are two chief banners'; = hay) · also ha — perfect auxiliary 'has' before the participle (ha vendido 'has sold'; fechos los ha ricos 'has made them rich') · also 'has, gets' (de señor non ha graçia 'he has no favor from a lord')
puerto: puerto — mountain pass (Latin portus; al puerto de Alucat 'to the pass of Alucat'; = puerto)
alucat: Alucat — place name, a mountain pass (puerto de Alucat; Pidal: today Olocau del Rey, west of Morella, Castellón)
dexado: dexar — left, left behind (past part.; = dejado)
saragoça: Saragoça — Zaragoza, city on the Ebro, seat of a Moorish kingdom (= Zaragoza)
e: e — and (= modern y) · also aver — I have (1st sg. present, apocopated form of he, perfect auxiliary: Espeso e el oro, 'I have spent the gold') · also aver — 'I will', the future auxiliary in a split future (quitarvos e … darvos e de mano 'I will free you … I will let you go'; = vos quitaré, vos daré) · also the full verb 'I have' (el sabor que dend e 'the delight I have of it')
a: a — to, at · also aver — he/she has (3rd sg. present, h-less spelling of ha, as in el rey me a ayrado = el rey me ha airado) · personal a before a direct object (salvest a Jonás; a ti adoro); a + inf. 'to, about to' (tornólas a catar); a tan grand sabor 'with so great pleasure'; a ojo 'in plain sight' · also a — 'into' (sacar a çelada 'to lure into ambush'); 'at, in' (a la çaga 'at the rear'); 'against' (dar salto a la çaga); dative 'to' (a mí dedes); haber a + inf. 'have to' (lo han a far); a + noun of direction (adeliñava a la puerta 'made for the gate') · impersonal 'there is' (aver; es dia a de plazo 'there is (only) a day of the term', the most likely reading of a hard line); ha as auxiliary set after the participle (soñado a 'he has dreamt') · also 'on, at (a time)' (a tercer dia 'on the third day') · also a — 'has' before the participle, agreeing with the object (la lança a quebrada 'he has broken the lance'; a menester 'has need of'); a + dative of the person affected (a Minaya matáronle el cavallo 'they killed Minaya's horse') · a — 'as, for' (tóvoslo a grand fonta 'he took it as a great affront')
las: el/la — the (fem. pl.); them (fem. object pronoun)
huesa: Huesa — Huesa, a town of the province of Teruel (Pidal), not Huesca (a Huesa e a Mont Alván; = Huesa)
mont: Mont — mount, hill (Latin montem; = monte); Mont Mayor, the place Martín Muñoz held: Montemayor, a Portuguese town he governed for Alfonso VI, according to Pidal · also Mont Real — Monreal, name of the place above which the Cid's hill stands (Pidal: Monreal del Campo, on the Jiloca); see real · also Mont Alván — Montalbán, town in Teruel (a Mont Alván; = Montalbán)
alván: Alván — Albán, as in Mont Alván, Montalbán, a town in Teruel (= Alván, in Montalbán)
contra: contra — toward, facing, in the direction of (= hacia; contra la sierra 'facing the sierra')
conpeçó: començar — he began (preterite 3rd sg.; conpeçó de espolonar 'he began to spur'; = comenzó)
sol: sol — sun · also 'even, so much as' (sol non 'not even'; sol non será penssado 'it will not even be thought of')
tornós: tornar + se — she turned back (tornó + -s(e): after a stressed vowel -se shrinks to -s) · also tornarse a + inf. 'to set to, begin' (tornós a sonrisar 'he broke into a smile', perhaps 'smiled again'; the Cid the subject)
part: part — share, portion (noun; = parte) · also part — side (del otra part 'on the other side'; = parte)
myo: mio — my (unstressed possessive, variant spelling of mio)
gañó: gañar — he won, captured (preterite 3rd sg.; = ganó)
que: que — that, who, which; for · also por que — because, since (= porque) · por que — by which, whereby (por que más valdrá 'whereby he will be worth more') · also que — 'so that, lest' introducing purpose/result (que por miedo non dexen nada; por tal lo faze … que no lo ventasse nadi); after después/mientra 'after, while' (después que, mientra que)
es: seer — it is (present 3rd sg.) · also ser as perfect auxiliary of intransitives (exido es 'has gone out') and passive auxiliary (la tienda es cogida)
en: en — in, into, on · en — of it, thence (= ende; por en avemos qué fablar 'of which we have to speak') · also en — 'as' (en paria 'as tribute'); en essora 'at that moment' · also en — 'among' (en todos los sos 'among all his men')
él: él — he (stressed subject pronoun) · also él — 'him, it' after a preposition, of a thing (a él vino; en él fincaredes 'in it', i.e. in Castejón)
todo: todo — all, every (de todo conducho, 'with every kind of provision')
priso: prender — he took (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = prendió, tomó)
ya: ya — O! (vocative particle, Arabic yā); also 'now, already' · also ya — 'would', reduced imperfect of aver as conditional ending, 3rd sg., after infinitive + clitic (pagar se ya 'would be satisfied'; = -ía)
dios: Dios — God · also Dios! — interjection of wonder (Dios, cómmo se alabavan! 'God, how they boasted!')
le: le — to him, him (dative pronoun) · also le — him, as direct object (leísmo; si ellos le prenden 'if they take him'); dative (non se le dava 'did not surrender to him')
iva: ir — he was going (imperfect 3rd sg.; iva posar 'was going to halt'; = iba) · ir + gerund, progressive 'was gradually doing' (yas iva alegrando 'was already cheering up'; miedo iva aviendo 'was going along with fear')
valençia: Valençia — Valencia, the Moorish kingdom and city whose king Tamín is addressed (= Valencia)
pesa: pesar — it grieves, it distresses (present 3rd sg., impersonal; mucho pesa a los de Teca 'it greatly grieves the men of Ateca'; = pesa)
los: el — the (masc. pl.); them (object pronoun) · also los que 'those who' (demonstrative use before a relative); los — him, them as object of consejar (commo los consejava 'as he advised them') · also los de 'those of' (con los de Castejón 'with the men of Castejón')
sabet: saber — know, mark you (imperative 2nd pl., sabed; sabet = sabed; epic tag addressed to the audience)
plaze: plazer — it pleases (present 3rd sg., impersonal; non plaze 'it does not please, they dislike it'; = place)
prisieron: prender — they took (strong preterite 3rd pl.; del castiello que prisieron 'of the castle they took'; = prendieron, closest tomaron)
so: so/su — his, her, its (unstressed possessive sg.; so çervicio = su servicio); also seer — I am (1st sg. present; = soy; so ayrado, 'I am in [the king's] ira') · lo so — 'what is his, his own' (neuter article + possessive; lo so puede menguar 'what is his may dwindle')
consejo: consejo — counsel, advice · also consejo — help, remedy (si non das consejo 'if you give no help'; Pidal 'si no nos das ayuda')
quel: que + le — who ... him (que + enclitic/elided le) · that ... to him (quel creçe conpaña 'that company grows for him')
çercar: çercar — to besiege, surround (infinitive; le van çercar 'they go to besiege him', ir + infinitive; = cercar)
noch: noche — night (apocopated form of noche; cf. anoch)
al: a + el — to the; al menos 'even the least' · also a + el standing for a + la before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel (al espada = a la espada) · also al — 'other thing, the rest' (neuter, Latin alius; de lo al non pienssan nada 'of anything else they think nothing'; distinct from a + el) · also a + el before an infinitive 'on, upon' (al exir de Salón 'on leaving the Jalón'; = al salir) · al 'the other thing, the rest' in al feredes adelant 'the rest you will do later'
man: man — morning (the short form, from Latin mane; = mañana)
tornan: tornar — they turn, go back (present 3rd pl.; tornan de castigar 'they go back to instructing'; = tornan)
fincar: fincar — to stay, remain (infinitive; = quedarse, closest quedar)
grado: grado — thanks (grado a … 'thanks be to …') · also grado — will, good will (de grado 'willingly, gladly'; de grado non avrié nada, 'of good will there would be nothing to be had') · en grado tener 'to be thankful for' (en grado vos lo tengo 'I thank you for it')
tí: tú — thee (stressed object pronoun; = ti, old accentuation)
padre: padre — father · el Padre santo, God the Father
spirital: spirital — spiritual (adjective; Padre spirital 'the spiritual Father', God the Father; Señor spirital 'spiritual Lord'; = espiritual)
somos: seer — we are (1st pl. of seer = ser)
tod: todo — all, the whole (apocopated before a vowel)
mal: mal — harm, hurt, ruin · mal — evil, in the prayer's sense (por end es salvo de mal 'therefore he is saved from evil') · also mal — adverb 'sorely, ill' (por cuer le pesó mal 'it grieved him sorely at heart') · also tener a mal — 'to take amiss' (non lo tenga a mal 'let him not take it amiss')
vino: vino — wine (noun); also venir — he came (strong preterite 3rd sg.; por en vino a aquesto, 'that is how he came to this pass')
si: si — if; si + subjunctive alone = 'if only …!' · si non — otherwise, if not (si non, do sopiéredes 'if not, wherever you learn'); si + future subjunctive 'if' (si nos falláredes 'if you find us') · also si — si'nulla = sin + nulla with -n assimilated before n- (si'nulla dubda 'without any fear' (or 'doubt'); = sin ningún miedo, sin ninguna duda)
nos: nos — we (subject pronoun; = nosotros) · also nos — us, to us (object pronoun; atorgar nos hedes 'you will grant us') · also reflexive 'ourselves' (nos partimos 'we part'); dative (la missa nos dirá 'will say for us') · also nos' — non + se (aun nos' van del campo 'they are still not leaving the field'; the apostrophe marks the elision)
derecho: derecho — right, justice; satisfaction owed (noun; derecho me avrá a dar 'he will have to give me redress'; = derecho)
lo: lo — him, it (object pronoun) · lo que perdedes 'that which you lose' (neuter antecedent of the relative) · also lo — neuter article 'what is' (lo to 'what is yours'); pleonastic 'it' (lo an, lo han a far; por tal lo faze 'for that reason he does it')
fazen: fazer — they make, give (present 3rd pl.; grand yantar le fazen 'they give him a great feast'; = hacen)
menos: menos — least, less · menos fallar — to find missing, to miss (de los sos menos non fallaron 'of their own men they missed no more than fifteen') · also a menos de — 'without, short of' (a menos de batalla non pueden den quitar 'short of a battle they cannot get clear of it')
lid: lid — battle, fight (fem. noun; lid campal 'pitched battle'; vençiemos la lid 'we won the battle'; = lid, now literary, closest batalla, combate)
mandados: mandado — message, news, report (pl.; here the tidings that spread; = mandados)
por: por — through, along, by, for · purpose, 'in order to' (por el reyno quitar 'to quit the kingdom'); por + inf. 'yet to be done' (tres an por troçir 'three remain to pass'); 'for, on behalf of' (por mio Çid) · also por — 'out of, because of' (por miedo 'through fear'); 'for (that reason)' (por tal lo faze 'he does it for that reason'); 'by way of' (por Guadalfajara); por + noun 'for the sake of' ; por coraçón 'willingly' · also 'for (a price)' (por quanto serié conprada 'for how much it would be bought'); 'by means of' (por carta 'by writ'); 'through, thanks to' (por mí ganaredes 'through me you will gain') · also por — 'on, during (a time)' (por aquesta mañana 'this morning'); 'by way of, through' (por medio de la llaña 'through the middle of the plain')
unos: uno — some (masc. pl.; unos … otros 'some … others')
desí: desí — from there, thence; thereupon (adverb, des + i 'there'; e desí arriba 'and from there upward'; = desde allí, después) · also desí — next, then in a series (desí a Molina 'next Molina')
acá: acá — here, hither (adverb; exidos somos acá 'we have come out to here'; = acá)
aquesta: aquesta — this (fem. sg., reinforced demonstrative; = esta, archaic aquesta)
campal: campal — of the field, pitched (adjective, from campo; lid campal 'a battle in the open field'; = campal)
pro: pro — worth, merit; de pro 'worthy, of good standing' · also pro — profit, advantage, benefit (grant pro les fazié 'he did them great good, was of great profit to them')
terçer: terçero — third (apocopated before a noun; al terçer día 'on the third day'; = tercer)
juntados: juntar — gathered, assembled (past part. masc. pl.; son juntados 'have assembled'; = juntados)
an: aver — they have (3rd pl. present of aver = han) · perfect auxiliary (passados los an 'they have passed'; la missa acabada la an 'they have finished'); an por troçir 'there remain to pass'; an ... ha far 'they have to do, are to do'
ora: hora — hour (= hora); en buen ora, part of the poem's honorific birth-formula, 'born in a good hour' · al ora 'at that very hour, then' (en ti crovo al ora)
nasco: nacer — he was born (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = nació)
fablar: fablar — to speak (infinitive; = hablar, note f-)
mesnadas: mesnada — household troop, band of followers (pl.; = mesnadas)
sí: sí — so, thus (optative particle, Latin sic; sí el Criador vos salue 'so may the Creator save you'; = así, no modern use as a particle)
vos: vos — you (object pronoun, polite/plural) · also subject 'you' (vos, que por mí dexades 'you who leave for my sake'); dative 'to you' (dar vos quiero vuestra part) · also reflexive/ethic 'you (yourselves)' (id vos en algara 'go off on a raid'); dative with an impersonal sense (si cueta vos fore 'if need befall you')
después: después — afterward, then · also después que — since, seeing that (causal; después que de moros fo 'since it came from Moors')
cristiandad: cristiandad — Christendom, the Christian people (= cristiandad; tan buen día por la cristiandad 'such a good day for Christendom')
fo: seer (and ir, which shares this preterite) — he/it was; went (preterite 3rd sg.; = fue, restored by Pidal as f[o]; of this part's three occurrences, fo entrado and fo acusado are periphrastic/passive ser + past part. constructions, while fo algo is a plain copula with a pronoun predicate, 'was something') · also commo fo tu voluntad, ca fo tu voluntad 'as/for it was your will' (ser + noun subject, 'it was'; Pidal restores f[o]) · also se fo acomendar 'went to commend himself' (ir); fo de noch 'it was night' (ser de + noun, 'night had come'); fo desenparada (passive, 'was abandoned') · also fo — went (ir; mañanas fo Minaya 'in the morning Minaya went'); fo de moros 'it came from the Moors' (ser de + noun of origin; Pidal restores f[o])
mas: mas — but · also mas — 'most' (superlative, = más; en todo lo mas alto 'on the very highest part') · also mas — 'more' comparative (que es mas ondrada 'which is more honored'; = más)
han: aver — they have (present 3rd pl.; = han); after an infinitive, the auxiliary of a split future (seervos han = os serán) · also han a + inf. 'they have to, are bound to' (mandado de so señor todo lo han a far); 'they hold, possess' (que moros las han) · also perfect auxiliary 'have' with a participle agreeing with its object (la ganançia que han fecha 'the booty they have made')
firme: firme — firm; used adverbially, 'firmly, securely' (= firmemente) · also firme' — firmes, 'firm, steadfast' (adjective plural, final s dropped; firme' son los moros 'the Moors are firm', i.e. still holding their ground)
mientre: mientre — adverb-forming suffix, 'in a manner' (Latin mente; fuerte mientre = fuertemente)
son: seer — they are (3rd pl.) · also son — perfect auxiliary of intransitives and passive auxiliary (todos son exidos 'have all gone out'; nombrados son; son derramadas 'are scattered')
passe: passar — it may pass, may go (present subjunctive 3rd sg.; que non passe por al 'let it not pass by other means, let it be done so'; = pase)
mañana: mañana — morning (a la mañana 'in the morning'; otro dia mañana 'next morning'; = mañana) · also mañana — early, soon (adverb/predicate; mucho es mañana 'it is too soon (to take back a man in disgrace after only three weeks)'; = pronto, temprano)
me: me — me, to me · also reflexive 'myself' (fata que yo me pague 'until I am satisfied')
armas: arma — weapon, arms (pl.; armas de lidiar 'weapons for fighting'; en armas 'in arms, armed'; = armas)
iremos: ir — we shall go (future 1st pl.; iremos adelant 'we shall go onward'; = iremos)
veer: veer — to see (= ver; two syllables) · also to review, inspect (troops) (mandó ve[e]r sus yentes 'had his men mustered'; Pidal: 'revistar')
aquella: aquel — that (fem. sg.; aquella mayor az 'that largest battle line'; = aquella)
almofalla: almofalla — encampment, host, army camp (Arabic al-maḥalla; = hueste, campamento)
commo: commo — as, like (spelling variant of como) · how, that, in the way that (commo sirva a doña Ximena 'how he is to serve doña Ximena'); like (commo la uña de la carne) · also commo si + imperfect subjunctive — 'as if' (commo si escapasse 'as if he were fleeing') · commo que 'as one who' (commo que ira a de rey … es echado 'as one who has the king's anger and is cast out')
exidos: exir — gone out (past part. masc. pl.; son exidos 'have gone out', ser as auxiliary; = salidos)
tierra: tierra — land, country; one's own land · earth (fezist çielo e tierra 'you made heaven and earth'; por tierra 'on earth')
estraña: estraño — extraordinary, remarkable, great (fem.; priessa much estraña 'a most extraordinary rush'; = extraña)
soldada: soldada — wages, pay (of a retained man; from sueldo)
qué: qué — what a …! (exclamative) · also qué — what? which? (interrogative pronoun/adjective, as in de qué será pagado, 'with what will he be satisfied') · indirect: que non sabe qué se far '(so that) she knows not what to do'; avemos qué fablar 'we have something to speak of' · also qué — how (exclamative before an adverb: qué bien pago 'how well he paid')
dixo: dezir — he/she said (strong preterite; x = sh-sound; = dijo)
minaya: Minaya — the title by which the Cid's kinsman Álvar Fáñez is called, usually explained as mi + anaya 'my brother'
álbar: Álbar — Álvar (personal name, Álbar Fáñez; = Álvar)
campeador: Campeador — the Battler, the Champion (the Cid's epithet, from campo 'field of battle')
dedes: dar — you may give (present subjunctive 2nd pl., old -edes ending; = deis)
çient: çient — hundred (apocopated before a noun; = cien)
más: más — more; e más 'and moreover' · non más 'no more, nothing more'; por que más valdrá 'whereby he will be worth more'
delant: delant — ahead, in front (apocopated adverb; = delante)
bien: bien — well · bien — good, benefit (noun; algún bien vos pueda far 'some good I may do you') · bien — very, quite, intensifying an adverb (bien çerca del agua 'very near the water')
dubda: dubda — doubt; also fear (sin dubda 'without fear', or 'without doubt, surely'; = duda)
i: e/i — and (variant of e before some sounds) · also i — there, therein (adverb, Latin ibi, like French y; meted i las fedes, 'put your pledged faith into it')
avrá: aver — he will have (future 3rd sg., syncopated; aver a + inf. 'will have to': me avrá a dar 'he will have to give me'; = habrá)
del: de + el — of the (contraction) · also del standing for de + la before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel (del albergada = de la albergada)
otra: otro — other (fem. sg.; del otra part 'on the other side', with el before a vowel-initial feminine noun, = de la otra parte)
campo: campo — field, open ground, field of battle (= campo; en el campo 'in the open field'; the element in Campeador) · campo de Taranz 'the plain of Taranz'
gelo: ge + lo — it to him/them (ge, ancestor of modern se, + lo; = se lo)
dicho: dezir — said (past part.; a dicho = ha dicho, 'he has said')
mucho: mucho — much, greatly · also mucho — very, intensifying a predicate (mucho es mañana 'it is much too early, too soon')
era: seer — it was (imperfect of seer = ser) · era + past part. 'had' (ser as pluperfect auxiliary with intransitives; Minaya assí era llegado 'Minaya had arrived')
piénssanse: pensar + se — they set about (present 3rd pl. + reflexive; piénssanse de adobar 'they set about getting ready'; = se ponen a)
armar: armar — to arm (infinitive; tornáronse a armar 'they set about arming'; = armar)
cada: cada — each, every (= cada; a cada uno 'to each one')
uno: uno — one; en uno = 'together, as one' · el uno ... el otro 'the one ... the other' (el uno es en paradiso, ca el otro non entró)
dellos: de + ellos — of them, from them (contraction)
far: far — to do (apocopated infinitive of fazer; = hacer)
va: ir — he/she goes (present 3rd sg.; = va); ir + gerund, 'to be (gradually) doing' · ir + infinitive 'goes to' (la manol va besar 'goes to kiss his hand', el Duero va passar 'goes to cross the Duero') · also va — 'there is, goes on' impersonal (¡Qué priessa va en los moros! 'what a stir there is among the Moors!')
nombre: nombre — name; por nombre 'by name, called' (= nombre)
d: de — of, with (elided form of de before a vowel, d'arena = de arena) · de — from (unos d'otros 'one from another')
santi: santi — saint (old form before a saint's name, from Latin sancti as in Sancti Iacobi, which survives fused in Santiago; santi Yagüe 'Saint James'; = santo, san)
feridlos: ferir + los — ferid 'strike!' (imperative 2nd pl.) + los 'them' (object pronoun split out); = heridlos
amor: amor — love; por amor de 'for the love of'
voluntad: voluntad — will, willingness; de voluntad e de grado, a doubled formula, 'willingly and gladly' · God's will (commo fo tu voluntad 'as was your will'); de toda voluntad 'with all one's heart'
ca: ca — for, because (Latin quia) · ca — perhaps 'but, whereas' (el uno es en paradiso, ca el otro non entró allá; the sense is uncertain)
roy: Roy — Ruy, short for Rodrigo (Roy Díaz = Rodrigo Díaz, the Cid)
diaz: Díaz — Díaz (patronymic 'son of Diego'; Ruy Diaz, the Cid's name, = Ruy Díaz; same as díaz, here without accent)
tanta: tanto — so many, so much (fem. sg. used collectively; tanta adágara 'so many a shield'; = tanta)
veriedes: veer — you would have seen (conditional 2nd pl.; = veríais; the minstrel's aside to the audience)
crebar: crebar — to break (infinitive; = quebrar); crebar albores 'dawn to break'
partes: parte — part, quarter, direction (pl.); de todas partes 'from every quarter'
moros: moro — Moor (masc. pl.); a moros nin a cristianos, 'to any living soul' (merism)
quieren: querer — they wish, are about to (present 3rd pl.)
maguer: maguer — although (a rare word, of Greek origin)
dar: dar — to give (infinitive; split future dar gelos [hemos] = se los daremos) · also dar salto 'to make a dash, sally' (salto davan); dar çevada 'to give barley, feed the horses'
piedes: pie — feet (old plural, Latin pedes; los piedes e las manos 'the feet and the hands'; = pies)
alcaz: alcaz — pursuit, chase (verbal noun of alcançar; en alcaz 'in pursuit'; modern alcance means 'reach', closest persecución)
fata: fata — until, as far as (variant of fasta; = hasta)
segudar: segudar — to pursue (infinitive; Pidal 'perseguir'; used as a noun, el segudar 'the pursuit'; no modern segudar, = perseguir, as a noun persecución)
tornar: tornar — to return; tornar palabra 'to answer a word' · also tornar — 'to give back' (tornar nos la ha doblada 'will give it back to us doubled'; infinitive + enclitic + ha, future); to turn (round), transitive (mandó tornar la seña 'he had the banner turned about')
entravan: entrar — they were entering (imperfect 3rd pl.; = entraban)
quanto: quanto — as much as, whatever (= cuanto) · quanto ella mejor sabe 'as best she can' (quanto + comparative 'as much as') · also 'how much' (por quanto serié conprada 'for how much it would be bought'); 'as far/fast as' (quanto pueden andar) · tanto quanto 'as long as'; por quanto … ha 'for all that there is' (por quanto en el mundo ha)
no: no — not (variant spelling of non) · also nos — to us (nos elided before lo: no' lo, 'to us it')
nuevas: nueva — news, tidings (fem. pl.; sus nuevas legavan 'his news was arriving'; = noticias, nuevas)
van: ir — they go (present 3rd pl.) · also ir + gerund 'keep going' (passando van 'they go on passing') · also ir + infinitive 'go to' (le van çercar 'they go to besiege him'; se van tornar 'they go back')
